this kind of brain-dead interpretation is why "science" news is so bad.

I'm not very scientific myself, but I'm really interested in science so I have to rely on this kind of article to get my regular fix. Can you give me any tips what to look out for when deciding the value of something like this? I'd be really interest to know what makes it bad so I can learn to read more critically in the future.

sure! the main problem is the conclusion in the headline is not consistent with the research, which is very common. the idea that genetics make someone more or less likely to develop certain conditions is sound but it's just a risk factor. the gene makes you more susceptible to the condition but does not cause it. if it were the cause, then the presence of that gene would lead to the condition - this is what the headline suggests and that is not the case.

regarding anorexia it will probably be shown to be gut-bacteria related one of these days. gut bacteria research is super interesting and revelatory right now - you should check into it.

this article really isn't that bad - honestly I skimmed it the first time haha. the important thing is to be skeptical of big conclusions on science articles because it's rare when those things happen - ironically those stories are usually not recognized properly in the media at the time, either. also, regarding science in general, "studies" and "published articles" are not always accurate, or even true. there is plenty of academic fraud and plenty of nefariously-motivated "science" out there. if you're interested over time you'll develop a better understanding of the general functioning of things and it'll be easier to sniff out what's important and what's bullshit. thinking for yourself is always the best way!
Thanks! So it's kind of the scientific news equivalent of clickbait? Figures, lol.
